If $Z_i\sim N(0,1)$ for $1\leq i \leq k$ are independent normal random variables, then the sum

$$
Z_1^2+Z_2^2+\cdots + Z_{k}^2
$$

follows a $\chi^2(k)$ distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom.

So, in our case, we have

$$
Y = Z_1^2+Z_2^2+\cdots + Z_{10}^2 \sim \chi^2(10).
$$

First, we express the given probability in the form $P(Y\geq y){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le y) & =1-P(Y\ge y) \\ 0.99 & =1-P(Y\ge y) \\ P(Y\ge y) & =0.01\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we wish to find the value $y$ such that $P(Y\geq y) = 0.01$ This can be found from the given table:

| $k \setminus p$ | $0.010$ | $0.050$ | $0.100$ | $0.150$ | $0.200$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $8$ | $\,20.090\,$ | $\,15.507\,$ | $\,13.362\,$ | $\,12.027\,$ | $\,11.030\,$ |
| $9$ | $\,21.666\,$ | $\,16.919\,$ | $\,14.684\,$ | $\,13.288\,$ | $\,12.242\,$ |
| $10$ | $\,\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}23.209}\,$ | $\,18.307\,$ | $\,15.987\,$ | $\,14.534\,$ | $\,13.442\,$ |

So, we have

$$
P(Y\geq 23.209) = 0.01
$$

which means

$$
P(Y\leq 23.209) = 0.99.
$$

Therefore, the value $y$ that satisfies $P(Y\leq y) = 0.99$ is $y=\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}23.209}.$
